mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny home permit and an ADU permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU (Accessory Dwelling Unit) permit is a specific type of permit that allows for the construction or placement of a secondary dwelling on a property, often encompassing tiny homes used for permanent living. Not all tiny homes are ADUs; for example, a tiny home on wheels used for recreational purposes might not fall under ADU regulations. However, most tiny homes intended for permanent occupancy on a foundation or with utility connections will typically require an ADU permit, especially in California, due to state laws encouraging their development.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU permit is for a secondary dwelling, often including tiny homes used for permanent living. Not all tiny homes are ADUs, but most permanent tiny homes require ADU permits.
